entity_types.business: The source's business/legal-person subject; legal form remains unknown unless stated.
entity_types.licence: An authorisation held by a business.
entity_types.establishment: A physical operating facility, separate from its operator.
entity_types.employer_reporting_unit: An employer reporting unit that submits WGEA Gender Equality Reporting results for a reporting year, identified by its reporting ABN; its legal form and company-wide scope are not established by this source.

ext.entity.former_name.definition: A legal name the business held before its current one. Use valid_from/valid_to paths when the source dates the name. Never a trading name.

ext.entity.legal_form.definition: Registrar's company type, decoded through a crosswalk table. Unknown codes -> unknown.

ext.entity.legal_form_detail.definition: Finer legal structure stated by the registrar (limited by shares/guarantee, listed, superannuation trustee, non-profit). Value is "CODE: label" from a crosswalk table.

ext.entity.status_detail.definition: The registrar's full status code and label ("EXAD: External administration"). The core entity.status enum stays coarse; distress codes live here.

ext.entity.date_established.definition: Founding / establishment date. Not a registration date.

ext.entity.sector_tag.definition: A source-stated activity or beneficiary tag, e.g. scheme acnc_purpose or acnc_beneficiary. Keep the publisher's wording.

ext.entity.industry_code.definition: ANZSIC 2006 division letter, subdivision, group or class, produced only through a reviewed crosswalk table from a source-stated activity (trade class, licence category, purpose). The raw source value is kept in raw_value. scheme = anzsic2006.

ext.entity.operating_region.definition: Where the business says it operates (service footprint), not where it is registered.

ext.entity.operating_country.definition: Country the business says it operates in, as the source writes it (one per observation).

ext.entity.tax_concession.definition: Tax-concession status stated by the regulator (Public Benevolent Institution, Health Promotion Charity).

ext.entity.responsible_persons.definition: Number of responsible persons (board size) the regulator reports.

ext.entity.financial_year_end.definition: Reporting-cycle end as dd-Mon (e.g. 30-Jun). Used to schedule refreshes.

ext.entity.prior_registration_state.definition: State of original incorporation before national registration. Not an address.

ext.entity.address_point.definition: lat,lon of the business's OWN stated address (e.g. a licensee's business address). A premises or site location is ext.establishment.geo on an establishment role instead.

ext.entity.holder_kind.definition: Whether the source says the record's holder is a natural person or an organisation. This is matching evidence. It never implies sole_trader.

ext.financial.total_income.definition: Total income as published for a stated reporting period. A fact for a period, not a current attribute.

ext.financial.taxable_income.definition: Taxable income for the period. Missing is not zero.

ext.financial.revenue_band.definition: A revenue/turnover band from a named scheme (acnc_size_2022, qbcc_mfr). The value must be a label of that scheme's crosswalk table; band thresholds live in the table, not in the claim.

ext.licence.number.definition: Publisher-assigned licence number. Identifies the licence across snapshots.

ext.licence.class.definition: Licence class / licensed trade in the publisher's wording.

ext.licence.category.definition: Licence category in the publisher's wording.

ext.licence.authorisation.definition: One authorised activity per observation (split the publisher's list).

ext.licence.authorisation_text.definition: Complete publisher authorisation text, including headings and conditions. Unparsed source evidence, not independent permission claims.

ext.licence.start_date.definition: Publisher-stated commencement of the licence, not the business establishment or registration date.

ext.licence.end_date.definition: Publisher-stated end of the licence, not the end of the business or all its claims.

ext.licence.status.definition: Licence status as published (licence status, not company status).

ext.licence.condition.definition: Licence condition such as trading hours.

ext.licence.status_event.definition: A dated status-history entry (e.g. a contravention of a licence condition).

ext.licence.related_licence_number.definition: Number of another licence the same holder holds (e.g. an AFS licence number). 0 / blank = none.

ext.establishment.source_key.definition: Publisher's site code. Identifies the site across snapshots.

ext.establishment.geo.definition: "lat,lon" in decimal degrees inside Australia. The literal NULL is missing.

ext.establishment.region.definition: Publisher's region (licensing region, metro/regional, employment services area).

ext.establishment.capacity.definition: Published maximum patron count or similar capacity.

ext.establishment.program.definition: Government programme or contract code delivered at this site.

ext.contact.phone.definition: Phone number normalised to E.164 (+61...). Numbers shorter than 8 digits or without an area code are rejected. Mobiles are personal data unless published as a business line.

ext.contact.email_domain.definition: The domain of a published email address. Personal local parts are never stored.

ext.contact.role_email.definition: A role mailbox (info@, enquiries@, admin@ ...). Personal mailboxes are dropped by the transform.

ext.contact.website_domain.definition: Registrable host of a published website (www. removed).

entity.legal_name.definition: As registered. Not the trading name.

entity.trading_name.definition: May be multiple. Emit one observation each.

entity.abn.definition: Australian Business Number. Has a checksum — validate it, do not just length-check.

entity.acn.definition: Australian Company Number. Also checksummed. The last 9 digits of an ABN are often the ACN, but not always.

entity.nzbn.definition: New Zealand Business Number, if you happen to hit an NZ source.

entity.entity_type.definition: Default to unknown. Guessing here causes downstream harm.

entity.industry_code.definition: ANZSIC where available. Record the raw source value too.

observation.source_id.definition: Stable identifier for the dataset the claim came from.

observation.source_record_id.definition: Must be traceable back to the exact raw record. If the source has no key, construct a deterministic one and document how.

observation.ingested_at.definition: When you read it. These are different and both matter.

observation.valid_from.definition: When the claim became true in the world, if the source says.

observation.valid_to.definition: Null means still current as far as this source knows.

observation.licence.definition: From the dataset metadata. CKAN exposes it. If a source has no clear licence, that is a finding, not a blocker — record 'unknown' and flag it.

observation.extractor_version.definition: Which version of your mapping config and engine produced this. You will be glad of it later.

confidence.source_reliability.definition: How much do we trust this publisher on this kind of claim.

confidence.field_confidence.definition: How sure are we that we mapped and parsed this field correctly.

confidence.link_confidence.definition: How sure are we that this record refers to that entity. Only on links.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.size_band.definition: The employer size range band reported for the WGEA submission, expressed as an employee-count band such as '<250', '250-499' or '5000+'. The band set is publisher-defined and open-ended at the top; it is a band, not an exact headcount.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.size_band.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents an employer headcount band; ext.financial.revenue_band is a revenue band under a named scheme and is not an employee-count band, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.anzsic_divis.definition: The ANZSIC division name the employer reporting unit reported for its WGEA submission, e.g. 'Transport, Postal and Warehousing'. It is the publisher's division label, not a coded ANZSIC value.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.anzsic_divis.why_not_existing: ext.entity.industry_code expects a coded ANZSIC value (division letter, subdivision, group or class) and is owned by business; entity.industry_code likewise expects a coded ANZSIC value for the business. This column holds a division name label for the reporting unit, so type, meaning and owner differ from both.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.anzsic_class.definition: The ANZSIC class name the employer reporting unit reported for its WGEA submission, e.g. 'Computer System Design and Related Services'. It is the publisher's class label, not a coded ANZSIC class number.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.anzsic_class.why_not_existing: ext.entity.industry_code expects a coded ANZSIC value and is owned by business; entity.industry_code likewise expects a coded ANZSIC value for the business. This column holds a class name label for the reporting unit, so type, meaning and owner differ from both.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.reporting_na.definition: The employer name as stated by the employer reporting unit in its WGEA Gender Equality Reporting submission for the reporting year. This is the reporting label, not a verified legal name or trading name, and is not a unique identifier.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.reporting_na.why_not_existing: entity.legal_name and entity.trading_name are owned by business and assert a legal/trading status this source does not establish; the value here is a reporting-unit label for a WGEA submission, so owner and meaning differ.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.reporting_ab.definition: The ABN the employer reporting unit used to identify itself in its WGEA Gender Equality Reporting submission. It is a reporting identifier for the reporting unit and does not by itself establish legal form or company-wide scope.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.reporting_ab.why_not_existing: entity.abn is owned by business and asserts the ABN of the business legal person; here the ABN is the reporting unit's submission identifier, so owner and scope differ even though the value format is the same.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.sector.definition: The sector classification the employer reporting unit reported for its WGEA submission, distinguishing private from public sector employers. It is a reporting classification, not a legal form.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.sector.why_not_existing: ext.entity.sector_tag is a source-stated activity/beneficiary tag requiring a scheme qualifier and is owned by business; this is a WGEA private/public sector classification of the reporting unit, so meaning and owner differ.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.total_workfo.definition: The share of the employer reporting unit's total workforce who were women, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.244 = 24.4%), not a whole percentage; it is a workforce composition share, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.total_workfo.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a female workforce composition share; ext.financial.revenue_band and the GPG concepts concern revenue bands and pay gaps, so reuse would change meaning. Owner is the reporting unit, not the business.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_quarti.definition: The share of the employer reporting unit's lower pay quartile who were women, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.75 = 75%), not a whole percentage; it is a composition share within a pay quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_quarti.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a female share within a pay quartile; the total-workforce share is a different population, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_middle.definition: The share of the employer reporting unit's lower-middle pay quartile who were women, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.38 = 38%), not a whole percentage; it is a composition share within a pay quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_middle.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a female share within a pay quartile; the total-workforce share is a different population, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_middle.definition: The share of the employer reporting unit's upper-middle pay quartile who were women, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.25 = 25%), not a whole percentage; it is a composition share within a pay quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_middle.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a female share within a pay quartile; the total-workforce share is a different population, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_quarti.definition: The share of the employer reporting unit's upper pay quartile who were women, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.16 = 16%), not a whole percentage; it is a composition share within a pay quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_quarti.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a female share within a pay quartile; the total-workforce share is a different population, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.total_workfo.definition: The average total remuneration in Australian dollars per employee across the employer reporting unit's total workforce, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Total remuneration is pay (base salary plus superannuation and other payments), not revenue or business income; the value is a pay level, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.total_workfo.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a remuneration level; ext.financial.total_income and ext.financial.taxable_income are business income measures owned by business, and the shortlisted GPG concepts are gaps, not dollar pay levels, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_quarti.definition: The average total remuneration in Australian dollars per employee within the employer reporting unit's lower pay quartile, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Total remuneration is pay, not revenue or business income; the value is a pay level for one quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_quarti.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a remuneration level for a pay quartile; the total-workforce average is a different population and the GPG concepts are gaps, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_middle.definition: The average total remuneration in Australian dollars per employee within the employer reporting unit's lower-middle pay quartile, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Total remuneration is pay, not revenue or business income; the value is a pay level for one quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.lower_middle.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a remuneration level for a pay quartile; the total-workforce average is a different population and the GPG concepts are gaps, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_middle.definition: The average total remuneration in Australian dollars per employee within the employer reporting unit's upper-middle pay quartile, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Total remuneration is pay, not revenue or business income; the value is a pay level for one quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_middle.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a remuneration level for a pay quartile; the total-workforce average is a different population and the GPG concepts are gaps, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_quarti.definition: The average total remuneration in Australian dollars per employee within the employer reporting unit's upper pay quartile, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Total remuneration is pay, not revenue or business income; the value is a pay level for one quartile, not a pay gap.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.upper_quarti.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a remuneration level for a pay quartile; the total-workforce average is a different population and the GPG concepts are gaps, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.average_base.definition: The average (mean) gender pay gap in base salary for the employer reporting unit, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.244 = 24.4%), not a whole percentage; a negative value indicates a gap favouring women. It is a pay gap, not a pay level or business income.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.average_base.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a gender pay gap; the shortlisted employer_reporting_unit concepts are workforce composition shares and remuneration levels, and ext.financial.total_income is business income owned by business, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.average_tota.definition: The average (mean) gender pay gap in total remuneration for the employer reporting unit, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Total remuneration is pay (base salary plus superannuation and other payments), not revenue or business income. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.244 = 24.4%); a negative value indicates a gap favouring women.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.average_tota.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a total-remuneration gender pay gap; the shortlisted total_workforce_average_total_remuneration is a dollar pay level, not a gap, and the base-salary gap is a different measure, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.median_base_.definition: The median gender pay gap in base salary for the employer reporting unit, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.069 = 6.9%), not a whole percentage; a negative value indicates a gap favouring women. It is a pay gap, not a pay level or business income.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.median_base_.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a median gender pay gap; the average base salary gap is a different statistic, and the shortlisted employer_reporting_unit concepts are composition shares and pay levels, so reuse would change meaning.

dyn.employer_reporting_unit.median_total.definition: The median gender pay gap in total remuneration for the employer reporting unit, as reported for the 2024-25 WGEA Gender Equality Reporting year. Total remuneration is pay (base salary plus superannuation and other payments), not revenue or business income. Stored by the publisher as a decimal fraction (0.069 = 6.9%); a negative value indicates a gap favouring women.
dyn.employer_reporting_unit.median_total.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept represents a median total-remuneration gender pay gap; the average total-remuneration gap and the median base-salary gap are different statistics, so reuse would change meaning.
